subject: Coffee & Tea
title: The Third Wave: Coffee as Craft
description: A micro-lesson that makes The Third Wave: Coffee as Craft usable.

hook.text: The 'third wave' treats coffee like wine—obsessing over origin, variety, processing, and the individual farmer who grew it.

buildup.text: First wave was commodity (Folgers). Second wave was café culture (Starbucks). Third wave elevates coffee to craft.

discovery.text: Third-wave roasters buy single-origin, traceable lots. They roast light to showcase terroir and score coffees like wine critics.

twist.text: Critics argue third wave is elitist—$7 pour-overs alienate everyday drinkers and ignore the global majority who drink instant.

climax.text: A possible 'fourth wave' focuses on equity—paying farmers fairly while making quality accessible, not just exclusive.

punchline.text: Commodity, culture, craft, equity. Each wave remakes what coffee means.

quiz.question: What defines third-wave coffee?
options: Treating coffee as artisanal craft — focusing on origin, variety, and terroir

details.summary: The third wave coffee movement treats coffee like craft wine, emphasizing single-origin sourcing, light roasting, and transparent supply chains. Emerging in the early 2000s, it values the farmer as much as the barista and seeks to highlight each coffee's unique terroir and processing.
details.whyItMatters: Third wave coffee redefined quality standards, created new markets for small farmers, and transformed coffee from a commodity into an artisanal experience.
takeaways: Third wave coffee emphasizes single-origin and traceability
Light roasts showcase origin character over roast character
Farmer recognition and fair compensation are core principles

faq.question: What distinguishes third wave coffee from first and second wave?
faq.answer: First wave made coffee a mass-market commodity. Second wave, led by Starbucks, introduced quality and cafe culture. Third wave treats each coffee as unique, emphasizing origin, process, and skill from farm to cup.

faq.question: How has the third wave movement changed things for coffee farmers?
faq.answer: It created direct trade relationships that pay farmers significantly above market rates. Farmers who produce exceptional lots can now earn premium prices at auctions, incentivizing quality over quantity and improving livelihoods.
